Title: Diagnosis of test `testIntersectionNotIntersecting`

Details:  
The test checks that two non-intersecting SubLine instances return null on intersection detection. The `SubLine.intersection(SubLine, boolean)` method handles this functionality. It relies on the intersection of the underlying infinite `Line` instances of each sub-line via `Line.intersection(Line)`. 

1. The method `SubLine.intersection` first computes the intersection point `v1D` of the infinite lines using `line.intersection(subLine.line)`.
2. The `Line.intersection` method internally calls `closestPoint` on one line to the other, which returns the closest point on the first line to the other line.
3. If this closest point lies on the second line (checked by `line.contains`), this point is the intersection; otherwise, null is returned.
4. The method `SubLine.intersection` then checks if this intersection point lies within the `remainingRegion` of each `SubLine`.
5. If the point is inside or on the boundary depending on the `includeEndPoints` flag, it returns the intersection point; otherwise, it returns null.

The failing test tries to find an intersection of two sub-lines that do not intersect. However, the `Line.closestPoint` method call indicates that if the two lines are parallel (detected by a small value `n < Precision.EPSILON`), it returns a zero vector unconditionally without any further checks (line 199: `return zero;`).

This can cause a problem if the line intersection is assumed to be the zero vector even when the lines are parallel and do not intersect. The zero vector could be falsely interpreted as a point on both sublines, which might cause the intersection check to incorrectly return a non-null value, causing the test to fail.

In essence, the bug is that `Line.closestPoint` returns the zero vector when lines are parallel without checking if this point really lies on either line or whether the lines overlap or not. This can lead the following `SubLine.intersection` method to falsely detect an intersection point for non-intersecting sublines.

The root cause lies in `Line.closestPoint(Line)` method's handling of parallel lines and subsequently the `Line.intersection(Line)` method.

Best locations to be fixed:
org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.Line.closestPoint(org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.Line)
org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.Line.intersection(org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.Line)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
